issues.summary: Test names, error message and doc comment still say 'current Safes' / 'Safe count' although the check now counts seats
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The interface defines a seat as one per Safe address across chains (space-safes.repository.interface.ts:80-84), so countSeatsBySpaceId is exactly the number of distinct Safes. That makes 'current Safes' (billing.service.ts:421, :442; spec :702, :731) more accurate than it was under the old per-row count, not less.

issues.summary: The PR/commit calls this a rename, but for billing it changes behaviour: rows were counted before, distinct addresses now, so the capacity check is looser for multi-chain Safes
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: countSeatsBySpaceId deduplicates per address (space-safes.repository.ts:216-224; interface :80-84), while the removed countBySpaceId counted rows. That makes billing.service.ts:437 a semantic change as well as a rename. The change is intended and matches #3446's seat rule, so what's off is only the description wording.

issues.summary: The seat-capacity tests never check which id countSeatsBySpaceId is called with
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The spec only stubs the return value (billing.service.spec.ts:714, :745, :968, :988), and no toHaveBeenCalledWith is used on the count mock. Passing the wrong id would therefore go unnoticed. The gap predates the PR, which only renamed these lines.

issues.summary: No billing test for a Safe on several chains counting as one seat
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: BillingService unit tests mock the count, so the multi-chain dedup belongs to the repository. #3446 already covers it in space-safes.repository.integration.spec.ts. A billing-level case would add little beyond checking that the right method is wired.
